## Methods Overview

Scripts referenced below are relative to the repository root `plant_immunity_Vitis/`.

### 1. Plant Material and Inoculum

*Plasmopara viticola* was obtained in June 2022 as a natural inoculum from Vinselekt Michlovský vineyards at the oil-spot stage.
Leaves were stored in the dark at 100% humidity and 22°C until sporulation; inoculum identity was confirmed by PCR and sequencing.
Spore suspensions were adjusted to 50,000 spores/ml (Cellometer K2).

In January 2022, one-year-old wood segments were collected from Vinselekt Michlovský vineyards and propagated under controlled conditions.
Three resistant genotypes carrying unique combinations of resistance loci — *Rpv12* (single), *Rpv12*+1 (double), and *Rpv12*+1+3 (triple) — were selected and verified by SSR markers linked to resistance loci (Hádlík et al., 2024).
Pinot Noir served as the susceptible control and fresh inoculum source.

At the five-leaf stage, 20 µl of spore suspension was pipetted onto the abaxial surface of three leaves per plant.
One-centimetre leaf discs were excised from the inoculation spot at 0, 6, and 24 hours post-inoculation (hpi) and stored at −80°C; three biological replicates (A, B, C) were collected per genotype × time combination, yielding **36 libraries** in total (4 genotypes × 3 time points × 3 replicates).

### 2. RNA Isolation and Sequencing

Total RNA was extracted using the Spectrum™ Plant Total RNA Kit (Sigma-Aldrich).
Concentrations were measured with SPECTROstar Nano; RNA integrity was confirmed with an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyser.
Library preparation and sequencing for all 36 samples were performed by Novogene (UK) on an Illumina NovaSeq platform (150 bp paired-end) across **two independent batches**.

### 3. Quality Control and Read Mapping

| Step | Tool | Version | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quality check | FastQC | 0.11.9 | Andrews S., 2010 |
| Adapter trimming | Trimmomatic | 0.39 | Bolger et al., 2014 |
| Read mapping | STAR | 2.7.4a | Dobin et al., 2013 |
| Count quantification | featureCounts (Subread) | 2.0.3 | Liao et al., 2014 |
| Gene annotation | BLASTp | 2.12.0+ | Johnson et al., 2008 |

Reads were mapped to the *Vitis vinifera* PN40024 v4 reference genome (ENSEMBL; 35,134 annotated protein-coding genes).
All 36 samples passed quality thresholds; 26,169 protein-coding genes were detected after filtering (≥15 total reads across all libraries).

Scripts: `01_QC_and_Filtering/Batch_effects/read_checks.R`

### 4. Batch Effect Detection and Normalization

Batch effects were detected by testing four read-mapping quality metrics (GLM + Spearman correlation, Benjamini–Hochberg FDR) between the two sequencing batches.
Three of four metrics differed significantly between batches (forward-only survival FDR = 0.003; dropped reads FDR = 0.004; reverse-only survival FDR = 0.014).

Two complementary normalization strategies were used depending on the analysis goal:

- **Size-factor normalization + log₂ + ComBat** (sva package; Leek et al., 2012): used for Aggregated Expression Divergence (AED). Preserves the full dynamic range of transcription amplitudes.
- **Regularized-log (rlog) + ComBat**: used for all correlation-based analyses (PCA, DGEA, co-expression network). Stabilizes mean–variance relationship; homoscedasticity confirmed by Spearman correlation of gene means vs variances (ρ ≈ −0.03 after rlog+ComBat).

PCA confirmed that after batch correction, PC1 (42.5% variance) separates genotypes rather than batches (Spearman ρ between PC1 and batch assignment: −0.104 for SF+ComBat, −0.137 for rlog+ComBat).

Scripts: `01_QC_and_Filtering/Batch_effects/batch_effects.R`, `02_Normalization_and_DGEA/Heteroscedasticity_check.R`

### 5. Differential Gene Expression Analysis (DGEA)

Batch-corrected rlog-transformed values were used for DGEA.
Because DESeq2 does not accept pre-corrected input, pairwise t-tests (Welch) were applied per gene for each resistant genotype vs the susceptible control at each time point.
P-values were adjusted using Benjamini–Hochberg FDR.

**DEG criteria:** |log₂FoldChange| > 1 AND FDR < 0.05

A total of **3,553 DEGs** were identified across all comparisons.

Script: `02_Normalization_and_DGEA/DGEA.R`

### 6. Gene Categorization and Grouping

Each DEG was assigned a temporal expression pattern based on its up/down/equal regulation at each time point (0, 6, 24 hpi) relative to the susceptible control:

| Category | Code | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| Initial Expression Variation | IEV | Change at 0 hpi (±0 and 6 hpi) |
| Early Response | ER | Change at 0 and 6 hpi |
| Transient Response to Stress | TRS | Change only at 6 hpi |
| Late Response | LR | Change at 24 hpi |
| Sustained Change | SCh | Change at all three time points |
| Complex Patterns | CPs | All other combinations |

Genes were further grouped by comparing patterns across genotypes (Groups I–VI):
Group I = shared by all three genotypes; Group II = *Rpv12* and *Rpv12*+1; Group III = *Rpv12*+1 and *Rpv12*+1+3; Group IV = *Rpv12* and *Rpv12*+1+3 (recovered); Group V = genotype-specific; Group VI = complex multi-genotype patterns.

### 7. Transcriptional Dynamics Modelling

Generalized linear models (negative binomial family, log link) were applied to DEG counts to test effects of genotype, infection time, and direction of regulation.
Pairwise contrasts used estimated marginal means with Tukey's HSD post-hoc tests (emmeans package).

Script: `05_transcriptional_dynamics/DEGs_counts_global_tests.R`

### 8. Aggregated Expression Divergence (AED)

AED quantifies the overall transcriptional distance of each resistant genotype from the susceptible reference at a given time point:

$$\text{AED} = \frac{1}{G} \sum_{g=1}^{G} \left(\bar{x}_{g,\text{resistant}} - \bar{x}_{g,\text{susceptible}}\right)^2$$

where $G$ = number of genes and $\bar{x}$ = mean log₂ expression across replicates (size-factor + ComBat values).

Statistical significance was assessed against a null distribution generated from all $\binom{12}{3} = 220$ random triplets of same-timepoint samples.
Empirical one-sided p-values were FDR-corrected across nine genotype–time comparisons (minimum attainable FDR = 0.024).

Script: `03_AED/DGE_bySFandCB_divergence.R`

### 9. Co-transcriptional Network Analysis (PCNWA)

Pairwise Pearson correlations were computed across the 3,553 DE genes using rlog+ComBat expression values.
Edges were retained above the 99.5th percentile of the correlation distribution (r > 0.817).
Co-transcriptional modules were defined for each DE gene as the set of genes with r ≥ 0.817; modules with ≥4 genes whose eigengene (first principal component) correlated significantly with the gene's temporal pattern (Spearman, Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.05) were retained (155 modules).
Hub genes = top 1% by degree centrality (56 hub genes; 117–1,552 partners).
Metamodules were derived by hierarchical clustering (complete linkage) of Euclidean distances based on shared hub-gene neighbourhood overlap.

Genotype-specific and time-specific networks were constructed separately using the same threshold.

Scripts: `06_PCNWA/GCNA_network_analysis.R`, `06_PCNWA/create_immunity_classes.R`

### 10. PTI/ETI Gene Classification

Immunity-related genes were identified by homology mapping of *Arabidopsis thaliana* immunity annotations to *Vitis vinifera* orthologs.
Genes were classified as ETI-specific, PTI-specific, or PTI–ETI shared based on literature-curated function.

Data file: `data_files/Vitis_gene_immunity_class.csv`

Script: `06_PCNWA/create_immunity_classes.R`

### 11. Gene Enrichment Analysis

Functional enrichment of GO terms, Reactome pathways, UniProt keywords, and protein domains used the STRING database (Szklarczyk et al., 2025) and PantherDB (Mi et al., 2013), queried with both *Vitis vinifera* gene IDs and *Arabidopsis* homologs.

### 12. Protein–Protein Interaction Prediction (AlphaFold2-Multimer)

Candidate immune receptor complexes were identified by systematic AlphaFold2-Multimer screening via ColabFold (Mirdita et al., 2022).
A total of **1,645 protein pairs** were tested, selected from 155 co-transcriptional modules and layer-specific DEGs.

ColabFold parameters: `--model-type alphafold2_multimer_v3 --num-models 5 --num-recycle 3`

High-confidence interactions required all four filters:

| Filter | Threshold |
|---|---|
| ipTM (interface predicted TM-score) | ≥ 0.7 |
| pLDDT (per-residue confidence) | ≥ 50 |
| Interface contacts (Cα–Cα ≤ 8 Å) | ≥ 5 |
| Contact-filtered PAE | < 10 Å |

Negative controls: transcription factors (PRE6, WRKY51, WRKY55, NAC29) and 325 cross-module protein pairs (0% hit rate).
Positive control: EDS1–SAG101 heterodimer (ipTM 0.79–0.89, PAE 4.79–6.93 Å).

Specificity of the EIX1–SOBIR1 interaction was further validated by comparing ipTM scores across eight co-localised membrane-resident proteins from orthogonal signalling pathways (EIX1, SOBIR1, FERONIA, WAK5, LAZ5, ACD6, RGA4, MIK2).
